bottleneck.description: Largest US ferrovanadium producer + global #1 spent-catalyst recycler (V-CYCLE) + titanium aluminide / aluminum master alloys to aerospace engines + AMG Technologies vacuum furnace equipment to engine forgers.

dependency.key_customers: Aerospace engine OEMs and forgers (via AMG Technologies furnaces and TAC master alloys), oil refiners (catalyst recycling feedstock), steel mills (ferrovanadium), tier-1 battery makers (lithium concentrate)
dependency.key_suppliers: Oil-refinery spent catalyst (long-term recycling contracts), Brazilian tantalum ore (AMG Brasil), Brazil lithium spodumene (Mibra mine), chrome ore

editorial.notes: AMG owns multiple niche-leadership positions: world's largest spent-catalyst vanadium recycler, largest US ferrovanadium producer (60kt/yr in Zanesville, OH), and a meaningful share of qualified titanium master alloys (AMG TAC Nuremberg) and chrome metal for nickel superalloys serving aero engine programs. Switching costs are real in aero-qualified master alloys and chrome metal for Ni-superalloys, but global ferrovanadium has Chinese and South African competitors and lithium/tantalum segments are not market-leading. Not HIGH because the portfolio is genuinely competitive at the alloy commodity level; not LOW because the spent-catalyst recycling and US ferrovanadium positions plus aero master alloy qualification provide real choke-point bite.
